t: This is the London School of Economics, a public research university and part of the University of London, specialising in the social sciences. It was founded by four people with strong links to the Fabian Society: Sidney and Beatrice Webb, Graham Wallas, and the playwright George Bernard Shaw. Beatrice Webb was a sociologist and social reformer who coined the term collective bargaining. Sidney Webb later wrote the original Clause Four for the Labour Party. Shaw, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925, is best known here as one of the founders.
